caption:
A nearby edge can serve a fresh cached image without another origin fetch. Follow /shoe.jpg through a miss, a fill, a hit and an expiry. Cache behavior depends on the key, freshness and response rules. Keep personal responses out of shared caches.

Inspect cache status and Cache-Control before comparing timings.
#systemdesign #beyondlocalhost
cover_title: Why fetch the same image twice?

takeaway: Inspect cache status on the image response
Compare Cache-Control and cache key rules
Test changed content and personal response handling

scenes.title: Same image. Different journey.
scenes.narration: The first image request waits on the origin. The next gets a fresh copy from the edge.
scenes.note: A fresh eligible cache hit avoids another origin fetch.

scenes.title: A stop near the viewer
scenes.narration: You open a product page and request shoe dot JPEG. A nearby CDN edge checks for a matching cached response.
scenes.note: One public image request, followed through one edge.

scenes.title: The shelf is empty
scenes.narration: On this cache miss, the edge asks the origin for the image. The origin returns the public, cacheable response.
scenes.note: MISS: the edge must fetch the image from origin.

scenes.title: Keep a permitted copy
scenes.narration: The edge stores that response when its cache rules allow it. The cache key and freshness rules determine later reuse.
scenes.note: Storage and reuse depend on configuration.

scenes.title: Same key. Fresh copy.
scenes.narration: A later request matches the same key while the copy is fresh. The edge serves it without another origin fetch.
scenes.note: HIT: a fresh copy can satisfy this request.

scenes.title: Freshness has a boundary
scenes.narration: When the copy expires, the edge may revalidate or fetch again. Purging a changed image also needs deliberate configuration.
scenes.note: An old copy is not an unlimited promise of freshness.

scenes.title: Personal data stays personal
scenes.narration: Your account response is different. Shared caching must respect private and no-store directives so personal data is not reused across users.
scenes.note: Honor response rules; do not force-cache personal pages.

scenes.title: Read the evidence
scenes.narration: Inspect cache status, compare response headers, and test a changed image. A nearby server helps only when the cache rules fit.
scenes.note: Check the actual response, not a promised speedup.
